([[Akron, Ohio]]) | college = [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 20 | draft_team = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]] | team2 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team3 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team4 = [[Cleveland Charge]] | years5 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team5 = [[Orlando Magic]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2022) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2022) * [[Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team (2022) * [[Ohio Mr. Basketball]] (2021) }} '''Malaki Lamar Branham''' (born May 12, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. ==Early life== Branham was raised in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. Starting in fifth grade, he trained under Jason Dawson in Columbus.{{Cite web |last=Hass-Hill |first=Colin |date=July 15, 2021 |title=Chasing Perfection: How Malaki Branham Went From A Gangly Fifth-Grader To Heralded Ohio State Freshman |url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2021/07/123564/chasing-perfection-how-malaki-branham-went-from-a-gangly-fifth-grader-to-an-ohio-state-freshman |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=Eleven Warriors}} He moved to [[Akron, Ohio]] where he attended high school at [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]].{{Cite web |last=Hass-Hill |first=Colin |date=July 22, 2020 |title=Q&A: St. Vincent-St. Mary Coach Dru Joyce Explains What Malaki Branham Brings To Ohio State |url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting/2020/07/115271/qa-coach-st-vincent-st-mary-dru-joyce-explains-what-malaki-branham-brings-to-ohio-state?amp |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=Eleven Warriors}} At St. Vincent–St. Mary, he won two state championships in 2018 and 2021.{{Cite web |title=2021-22 Men's Basketball Roster – Malaki Branham |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/malaki-branham/4295 |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=Ohio State Athletics}} He was named first team All-Ohio in his junior and senior seasons.{{Cite web|url=https://ohsaaweb.blob.core.windows.net/files/Sports/Basketball-Boys/2019-20/2020OPSWAAll-OhioBoysBKBTeams.pdf|title=2020 OPSWA All-Ohio Boys Teams|website=OHSAA.org}}{{Cite web|url=https://ohsaaweb.blob.core.windows.net/files/Sports/Basketball-Boys/2020-21/BoysBasketballAll-OhioTeam2021.pdf|title=All-Ohio Boys Teams|website=OHSAA.org}} As a senior, Branham averaged 21.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.8 steals per game. In his senior season, he was named [[Ohio Mr. Basketball]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohsaa.org/Sports/News/malaki-branham-named-ohio-mr-basketball|title=Malaki Branham Named Ohio Mr. Basketball|website=OHSAA.org}} and made the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], which was not played due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web |last=Lind |first=Andrew |date=May 22, 2021 |title=2021 Ohio State Basketball Signee Malaki Branham Named To Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://www.si.com/college/ohiostate/recruiting/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting-2021-guard-signee-malaki-branham-named-to-jordan-brand-classic |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=Buckeyes Now FN}} Branham was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked as the best player in Ohio. On July 22, 2020, Branham committed to playing college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from teams such as [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=July 22, 2020 |title=Top-30 prospect Malaki Branham commits to Ohio State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29517759 |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}} {{College Athlete Recruit February 26, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Malaki Branham Eli Brooks.jpg|thumb|left|Branham guards [[Eli Brooks]] in 2022]] Branham started his college career off the bench, but quickly became a regular starter.{{Cite web |last=Strom |first=Griffin |date=January 11, 2022 |title=Malaki Branham Continues To Look Like True Second Option For Ohio State Amid Impressive Three-Game Run |url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2022/01/128605/malaki-branham-continues-to-look-like-true-second-option-for-ohio-state-amid-impressive-three-game-run?amp |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=Eleven Warriors}} He scored a career-high 35 points in a 87–79 overtime win against [[2021–22 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] after a nearly month-long COVID pause.{{Cite web |last=Jardy |first=Adam |date=January 4, 2022 |title=Ohio State's Malaki Branham enjoys 'Welcome to Star City' in Nebraska |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/2022/01/04/ohio-state-basketball-malaki-branham-shines-nebraska/9075525002/ |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}} In a three-game stretch in February, he scored 22, 27 and 31 points.{{Cite web |last=Stano |first=Ryan |date=February 25, 2022 |title=Ohio State basketball fans nervous about Malaki Branham |url=https://scarletandgame.com/2022/02/25/ohio-state-basketball-fans-nervous-malaki-branham/ |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=ScarletAndGame.com}} As a freshman, he averaged 13.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and two assists per game. Branham was named [[Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year as well as third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]].{{cite press release |title=2021–22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |date=March 8, 2022 |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |access-date=March 8, 2022 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |archive-date=March 8, 2022}} On April 1, 2022, Branham declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=April 1, 2022 |title=Ohio St.'s Branham enters draft, but may return |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33647890 |access-date=April 1, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |last=Jardy |first=Adam |title=2022 NBA draft: Ohio State's Malaki Branham says goodbye to Buckeyes |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/04/27/malaki-branham-leaving-ohio-state-nba-draft-2022/9549272002/ |website=[[The Columbus Dispatch]] |access-date=April 29, 2022 |date=April 27, 2022}} He was projected as a potential lottery pick in the draft. ==Professional career== ===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2025)=== Branham was selected with the 20th overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Spurs select Jeremy Sochan, Malaki Branham and Blake Wesley in 2022 NBA draft|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-select-jeremy-sochan-malaki-branham-and-blake-wesley-in-2022-nba-draft|date=June 23, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 23, 2022}} Branham joined the Spurs' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team.{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612759/spurs |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In his Summer League debut, Branham scored fifteen points in a 99–90 loss to the [[2022–23 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs vs Cleveland Cavaliers Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/sas-vs-cle-1522200004/box-score#box-score |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On July 8, 2022, Branham signed a rookie-scale contract with the Spurs.{{Cite web |last=Pederson |first=Landon |date=July 8, 2022 |title=Spurs Sign 2022 First Round Draft Pick Malaki Branham |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2022-first-round-draft-pick-malaki-branham |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} He made 66 total appearances (including 32 starts) for San Antonio during his rookie campaign, averaging 10.2 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Malaki Branham 2022–23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4565201/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Branham played in 75 games (including 29 starts) for the Spurs during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 9.2 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=Malaki Branham 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4565201/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 47 appearances off of the bench for San Antonio in the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], posting averages of 5.0 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Malaki Branham 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4565201/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Washington Wizards (2025–2026)=== On July 9, 2025, Branham and [[Blake Wesley (basketball)|Blake Wesley]] were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Kelly Olynyk]].{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Kelly Olynyk|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-aquire-kelly-olynyk|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2025|access-date=July 9, 2025}} Branham made 28 appearances for Washington during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 4.6 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Malaki Branham 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4565201/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On February 5, 2026, Branham was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-malaki-branham-from-wizards-in-three-team-trade|title=Hornets Acquire Malaki Branham From Wizards In Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}} On February 9, Branham was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web |title=Hornets Waive Malaki Branham {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-malaki-branham |website=hornets.com |access-date=9 February 2026 |language=en}} ===Cleveland Charge (2026)=== On March 9, 2026, Branham signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web|title=Former Ohio State standout Malaki Branham joining Cleveland Charge|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/former-ohio-state-standout-malaki-224847745.html|access-date=March 13, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ===Orlando Magic (2026–present)=== On September 3 2026, Branham signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agents Malaki Branham and JD Davison |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agents-malaki-branham-jd-davison-20260903 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 3, 2026 |date=September 3, 2026}} ==Career statistics==
